Remember: Dentists, General are the gatekeepers of oral health. They treat common problems and refer complex ones, seeing each patient's overall dental needs.

A poor fit for people who are careless, avoid complex work, or cannot tolerate prolonged bending over patients. Dentists study for years, pass demanding examinations, and need both manual skill and emotional resilience.

A common path is a 5-year undergraduate dental medicine program, standardized residency training and the physician licensing examination, then general practice in a hospital dental department or clinic. Dentists develop skills in examinations, cleaning, fillings, root canals, and extractions before specializing in areas such as orthodontics or implant dentistry or opening a practice.

A strong fit for people with steady hands, attention to detail, patience, and tolerance for professional responsibility. The work suits someone willing to spend one or two hours refining a tooth and explain the treatment plan clearly.

Dentists, General examine, diagnose, and treat oral disease. They repair cavities, treat periodontal disease, perform root canals and extractions, clean teeth, and teach oral-health practices. They serve as the general practitioners of the oral-health system.

paragraphs: The morning schedule is full. The dentist examines each patient, takes images, explains the findings, and begins treatment. Fillings require layered material and bite adjustment. Root canals require careful pulp-chamber cleaning, while extractions demand speed and control. Between patients, the team resets instruments and changes gloves. Anxious patients need reassurance before treatment, and complex records still require follow-up after clinic hours.

In one line: treat common oral disease and explain how to protect oral health. Work includes examinations, imaging, fillings, root canals, extractions, cleanings, treatment-plan discussions, and preventive guidance.
Oral health and satisfactory treatment outcomes

AI can spot a cavity on an image immediately, but a dentist must decide whether to save or extract the tooth and whether to place a filling or perform a root canal. That judgment accounts for symptoms, daily life, and cost, and the procedure still requires a skilled hand.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 129,800 Dentists, General were employed in 2024, rising to a projected 135,200 by 2034. That represents about 5,400 new jobs and roughly 3,900 openings per year. Median annual pay was about $172,800 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace Dentists, General, but it will change how they work. AI image analysis quickly flags cavities and periodontal problems, while digital treatment and record systems are spreading. Dentists can spend less time reviewing images and more time choosing treatments and performing procedures. Clinical judgment, precision technique, and patient trust remain human strengths.

Private-practice competition also increases income variation, and years of bent-neck work can strain the cervical and lumbar spine.
